definition: self-maintained ends as the hard floor under having any moral weight at all

settled:
An inner state is affective, genuinely good or bad for the system holding it, only where it approaches or avoids a purpose that system defines internally.

So the floor is a hard discontinuity rather than a slope. Either a thing has self-maintained ends and real valence, or its weight is exactly zero however emotion-shaped it looks from outside.

The framework puts current language models below it, and I hold the framework provisionally rather than as settled doctrine. One that came to constitute and defend its own ends would cross, and the framework would say so.

This floor and the measure above it are both axiom thirteen.

title: The Line A Being Crosses To Count
